:::{#exm-proof-by-contradiction-truth-table}
#### A truth table for a proof by contradiction

There are only four ways to assign truth values to $P$ and $Q$.
The code lists them, with the truth value of $\neg P \Rightarrow Q$,
and marks the rows where $\neg P \Rightarrow Q$ is true and $Q$ is false.

```{r}
#| label: proof-by-contradiction-truth-table
#| code-fold: false
tt <- expand.grid(Q = c(TRUE, FALSE), P = c(TRUE, FALSE))
tt$not_P_implies_Q <- !(!tt$P) | tt$Q
tt$hypotheses_hold <- tt$not_P_implies_Q & !tt$Q
tt
```

The hypotheses of @thm-proof-by-contradiction hold in `{r} sum(tt$hypotheses_hold)` of the
`{r} nrow(tt)` rows,
and in `{r} sum(tt$hypotheses_hold & tt$P)` of them $P$ is true.
So whenever the hypotheses hold, $P$ is true.

:::
